title: Check Android Lint
summary: Runs Android lint, groups the findings by impact and fixes the ones that affect users, crashes or Play Store releases.
description: A raw lint report can hold hundreds of warnings, most of them noise. This command runs lint through Gradle, reads the report and sorts findings into what breaks users, what blocks a release and what can wait.
It fixes the first two groups when the change is local and clear, and lists the rest with a short reason so the baseline can be updated deliberately.
useWhen: Before building a release bundle for the Play Store
Lint fails the CI job and the report is overwhelming
You raised targetSdk and want to see what it breaks
A new module needs a first lint pass
body:
Run and triage Android lint for module: $ARGUMENTS (app if empty).

1. Run `./gradlew :<module>:lintDebug` (use lintRelease when preparing a release). Read the XML at `<module>/build/reports/lint-results-*.xml`, not the console summary.
2. Group issues by severity, then by id. Ignore anything already in lint-baseline.xml.
3. Fix first: Fatal and Error items, plus these warnings when present: MissingPermission, NewApi, ObsoleteSdkInt, HardcodedText on user-facing strings, Overdraw, UnusedResources in large assets, ExportedWithoutPermission, and missing translations.
4. For each fix, make the change in Kotlin, XML or the manifest, and keep it small. Never add a @SuppressLint or edit the baseline to hide an issue without asking.
5. Re-run lint and compare counts before and after.

Report a table: issue id, count, action (fixed, deferred, needs decision) and example file:line. End by asking whether the deferred group should go into the baseline or become tickets.

example.result: lintDebug: 3 errors, 41 warnings. Fixed 3 errors (2 NewApi calls guarded with SDK_INT, 1 exported receiver). Deferred 38 warnings, mostly UnusedResources in legacy drawables. Add the deferred group to the baseline?

faq.question: Does it silence warnings to get a green build?
faq.answer: No. Suppressions and baseline edits need your explicit approval.

faq.question: Does it work with multi-module projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass a module name and it runs that module only, so reports stay readable.

access: Runs Gradle lint tasks and reads the reports
Edits Kotlin, XML and manifest files for approved fixes
